mcqs.question: Which of the following best describes a random experiment in probability?

options.A: A process that always gives the same result each time it is performed
options.B: An experiment whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is performed
options.C: An experiment that has only one possible outcome
options.D: A process that does not involve any trials

mcqs.answer: An experiment whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty before it is performed
mcqs.explanation: A random experiment is one in which the result of each trial is uncertain; we cannot know in advance which outcome will occur. Option B captures this definition. Option A describes a deterministic process, C is incorrect because a random experiment has many possible outcomes, and D is vague and does not define randomness.

mcqs.question: When a fair coin is tossed twice, which of the following is an outcome of the experiment?
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is a single possible result of the whole experiment. Tossing a coin twice can give results such as HH, HT, TH, TT. "Heads then Tails" (HT) is one complete outcome. Options A and B are only single‑toss results, not full outcomes of the two‑toss experiment, and D is not an outcome but a probability value.

mcqs.question: In probability theory, an event is best defined as:

options.A: A single outcome of the experiment
options.B: A set of one or more outcomes of the experiment
options.C: The numerical chance that an outcome occurs

mcqs.answer: A set of one or more outcomes of the experiment
mcqs.explanation: An event is any collection (set) of outcomes from the sample space. It may contain one outcome (a simple event) or many (a compound event). Option B states this precisely. Option A describes a single outcome, not an event. Option C refers to probability, not the event definition, and D is the experiment, not an event.

mcqs.question: A die is rolled 60 times and the face ‘5’ appears 12 times. What is the experimental probability of obtaining a ‘5’?
mcqs.explanation: Experimental probability = (number of favorable outcomes) / (total number of trials). Here, favorable = 12, total = 60, so the probability is 12/60 = 0.20. Option B gives this fraction. Option A is the theoretical probability (1/6 ≈ 0.1667), C and D are unrelated fractions.

mcqs.learning_point: Compare experimental frequencies with expected likelihood
mcqs.question: A card is drawn from a standard 52‑card deck, the experiment is repeated 52 times, and the ace of spades is obtained 5 times. Which statement correctly compares the experimental frequency with the theoretical probability of drawing an ace?

options.A: The experimental frequency is greater than the theoretical probability
options.B: The experimental frequency equals the theoretical probability
options.C: The experimental frequency is less than the theoretical probability
options.D: The experimental frequency cannot be compared with the theoretical probability

mcqs.answer: The experimental frequency is greater than the theoretical probability
mcqs.explanation: Theoretical probability of drawing any ace = 4/52 = 1/13 ≈ 0.0769. Experimental frequency = 5/52 ≈ 0.0962, which is higher. Hence option A is correct. Option B would be true only if the counts matched exactly, C is false because 0.096 > 0.0769, and D is incorrect because comparison is straightforward.

mcqs.question: A teacher wants to select a student at random from a class of 30 to answer a question. Which of the following procedures correctly describes a random experiment?

options.A: The teacher always picks the tallest student
options.B: The teacher closes his eyes, mixes the names in a box, and picks one name without looking
options.C: The teacher selects the class monitor every time
options.D: The teacher counts the students from left to right and always chooses the 10th

mcqs.answer: The teacher closes his eyes, mixes the names in a box, and picks one name without looking
mcqs.explanation: A random experiment must give each possible outcome an equal chance and be unpredictable. Mixing names and picking blindly satisfies this. Option A and C are deterministic choices, and D always selects the same position, so none are random.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about outcomes is FALSE?

options.A: Each outcome is a possible result of the experiment
options.B: Outcomes can be combined to form events
options.C: Outcomes are the same as events
options.D: All outcomes are listed in the sample space

mcqs.answer: Outcomes are the same as events
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is a single result, while an event is a set of one or more outcomes. Therefore, saying they are the same is incorrect. Options A, B, and D correctly describe outcomes and their relationship to the sample space.

mcqs.question: Let event A be ‘getting a number greater than 4 when a die is rolled’ and event B be ‘getting an even number’. Which statement is true?

options.A: A and B are mutually exclusive
options.B: A is a subset of B
options.C: B is a subset of A
options.D: A and B are independent events

mcqs.answer: A and B are independent events
mcqs.explanation: A = {5,6}, B = {2,4,6}. Their intersection is {6}. P(A)=2/6=1/3, P(B)=3/6=1/2, P(A∩B)=1/6. Since P(A)·P(B)=1/3·1/2=1/6 = P(A∩B), the events are independent. They are not mutually exclusive (they share 6), and neither is a subset of the other.
